answer: A harbor keeps one beacon per agent, and each beacon burns behind a lens cut from nebula glass, a milky pane no two lenses share. Every epoch the keeper flashes a short cipher, a code the harbor master reads off the lens pattern and checks against the logbook. A copied beacon fails because its flash arrives at the wrong second and its cipher reads wrong against the registered pattern, and a moved lamp goes dark in the registry. A thousand fake names need a thousand working beacons, a thousand nebula lenses, and a thousand ciphers flashed on time.
